chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: How the Massey Hall concert came together
summary: Promoter in Toronto, Celia's role, Mingus's company recording Parker and Dizzy; Bird showed up after all.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Tell me, just to change the subject entirely, but since you mentioned it, what -- why don't you sort of fill us in on the details of that Massey Hall concert, how that happened to be? Who got the gig for that? You were the leader of that band, weren't you?

No. I can't think of the name of the guy. (inaudible) he wanted to book us to Japan. Yeah, Montreal. In Canada, You remember, Sue, Anyway, -- I think he lives in Toronto. Anyway, he called and said he wanted to get in touch with Dizzy Gillespie and Bud Powell, he wanted to use certain people. And I

think Dick Water was his name. My wife Celia really got it together. I didn't call nobody. I had a company and Max Roach decided to join it, and put the money up to record Charlie Parker, and Dizzy, at Jazz at Massey Hall. That was all.
Is it true that Dizzy -- I heard you had some problems getting there. I heard that Bird got lost or lost his horn or something like that.
No. We were all waiting, but he made it.
Well, that's good. I heard there was some tension with --
That's right, Dizzy brought Bird. He was about to not make it, I think, or something like that.
But then Dizzy was clowning on the band-stand behind Bird's solo or something like that, and Bird got angry or something like that?

He was saying, 'Salt peanuts,' and yelling and screaming. But Dizzy had a commercial band then. 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot,' was a hit for him. So he was clowning a lot. But Bird get mad? No, man. I got mad at Dizzy. He pulled his knife on me. Because Bird told me to take a solo and Dizzy came in.
